checks.check: For a finite bipartite relation with source supplies u, target capacities c, and uncapacitated relation arcs, max-flow/min-cut gives saturation iff u(X) <= c(N(X)) for every source subset X. Weighted neighborhood coverage is submodular; subtracting modular u preserves submodularity. Finite submodular minimizers are closed under union and intersection. This is only a feasibility criterion for the stated network.

For an invariant relation between transitive vertex orbits, any nonempty orbit-pair relation is biregular. A quotient flow amount on that orbit pair can be spread uniformly over its edges, giving equal per-vertex loads f/|U_i| and f/|L_j|. Quotient aggregate supply/capacity bounds then give literal per-vertex feasibility; the reverse direction follows by aggregation. Integer literal capacities yield integral flow. Tree automorphisms preserve original leaves, supports, selector membership, weights, and legal moves.

The route's stated non-implication is appropriately limited: an unweighted one-step subset-shadow result does not alone establish weighted neighborhood inequalities for a relation that also contains switches inserting a vertex absent from the source set. A separate bridge would be needed. The citation is not used here to prove a positive tree result.
